A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CaPL research. All 11 pages of each, including equations, tables, figures and references, support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original CaPL recognition results in Tables 1–3, ablations in Tables 4–7, and visual analyses in Figures 5–6.

after.justification: v4 retains these original CaPL experiments, ablations and visual analyses; retained results qualify as original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same BBDM attribute disentanglement, factual and counterfactual granules, losses, alternating training and cosine-similarity inference. The corrected ablation label does not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 11 recognition datasets for base-to-new generalization and cross-dataset transfer, plus ImageNet-V2, -S, -A and -R for cross-domain evaluation (Tables 1–3).

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical comparator membership within each task. The alternative disentanglement methods and query-initialization methods in Tables 5–6 also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same base/new class division, 16-shot training, accuracy metrics, frozen ViT-B-32 backbone and training settings. No evaluation procedure is added or revised.

E4.justification: The component, optimization, initialization and hyperparameter ablations and visual analyses are unchanged. Table 4 renames 'CaPL w/o UNI' to 'CaPL w/o FAC', matching the factual-intervention ablation already described in v1 Section 4.3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Single-value result reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–7 and qualitative findings in Figures 5–6 are unchanged. Table 4's relabeled ablation retains Base 77.32, New 73.58 and H 75.40.

T1.justification: The causal graphs, BBDM equations, attribute-query definitions, prediction probabilities and loss formulations in Section 3 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain identical claims about causal visual granulation, fine-grained discrimination and superior recognition performance across 15 datasets.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 retains the same mechanism explanations and interpretations of the ablations and visualizations. The limitation concerning longer BBDM training and the discussion of prompt-only inference are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including two-layer MLPs, a U-Net transfer model, T=1000, K=10, batch size 64, loss weights and the staged epoch schedule. No resource-access or other reproducibility information is added.

R1.justification: Section 2's discussion of global and local prompt learning, the positioning of CaPL against prior methods, and all 64 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 corrects 'As is seeb' to 'As is seen' in Section 4.2, aligns Table 4's abbreviation with 'FAC', and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 4's row label changes from 'CaPL w/o UNI' to 'CaPL w/o FAC'. The six figures, seven table structures, captions and placement otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Replacing the undefined 'UNI' label with 'FAC' in Table 4 resolves its inconsistency with Section 4.3 and clarifies which component the ablation removes. Together with the typo correction, this modestly improves clarity; the methods, evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
